inventory.name: RetryPolicy / TaskOutcome
inventory.purpose: Per-task retry discipline (§17.5): attempt 1 primary, attempt 2 same params, attempt 3 caller-supplied reduced-scope fallback to primary if none given. No backoff by design. Tracks session-wide failure count; after 3 total task failures (default threshold), all further run() calls short-circuit to MISSION_ABORT without executing.

inventory.name: SessionLogger
inventory.purpose: Per-session logging: date-hierarchical logs/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<id>/ directory holding session.db (SQLite, WAL mode, single connection), turns.jsonl (full-fidelity per-turn in/out dump), summary.md (Historian-authored or logger's own default stub). begin_turn/end_turn/log_event/finalize (idempotent) API.

inventory.name: RepetitionDetector
inventory.purpose: Live sliding-window (default 50 tokens) SHA-256 hash loop detector; fires a callback exactly once when the current window's hash matches recent history (default depth 8). Purely observational — does not kill anything itself.

inventory.name: NgramLoopFailureDetector
inventory.purpose: Distinct, POST-HOC forensic classifier (§17.2) applied only to a completed response that hit max_tokens: Jaccard n-gram similarity between the last 200 and preceding 200 tokens; >=0.60 similarity = loop-failure verdict, used to disqualify a model at tryout time (vs. a mere timeout, which doesn't disqualify).

inventory.name: HeartbeatMonitor
inventory.purpose: Background-thread timeout watchdog scoped to one generation call: fires on_timeout if the gap between beat() calls exceeds window_seconds (default 30s). Must be stop()'d explicitly or it leaks a thread.

inventory.name: ResourceWatchdog
inventory.purpose: Periodic RAM/CPU/disk/Ollama-health sampler; writes service-health.json every interval and fires on_alert when RAM crosses 85% or Ollama stops responding. RAM read via stdlib ctypes (Windows)/proc-meminfo (Linux) — no psutil dependency.

inventory.name: Guardrails / GuardConfig / GuardResult
inventory.purpose: IO-boundary path policy enforcement (§5): every file read/write must pass check_read()/check_write(). Excluded-pattern match is absolute (REJECT, no approval override). Writes additionally require an explicit truthy approval marker even on allowed paths. Ambiguous/unlisted paths REJECT by default policy. Refuses to construct at all if config/paths.yaml is missing (fail-closed, no implicit open-door default). Config hot-reload is deliberately manual (refresh()).

inventory.name: HierarchyEnforcer / Violation / EnforcementContext

promises: Router: exactly one local-model inference call runs at a time system-wide (Golden Rule 10); priority order OPERATOR_INTERACTIVE > VALIDATOR_RESPONSE > CRITICAL_MISSION > BACKGROUND, FIFO within a priority tier; a running call is never preempted mid-call; items that wait past their timeout are dropped rather than run stale; defensive checks refuse to spawn a second worker thread even across a stuck shutdown.

Eligibility: a model with unknown/unexposed context length is classified INELIGIBLE_MISSING_CONTEXT, never silently ELIGIBLE (explicit fail-closed fix, documented 2026-04-28); Claude-family models are categorically barred from the local_witness_validator seat regardless of measured capability; a model's claimed context is cross-checked against a computed KV-cache RAM ceiling, not trusted at face value.

Failover: detection is strictly separated from action — this module only ever produces a FailoverVerdict describing which of 4 signals fired; it never itself switches War Room into Autonomous Mode. Every detection check fails CLOSED (treated as 'cannot confirm Claude is alive') on any inability-to-check, rather than the previous fail-open default.

Retry: every task gets exactly 3 attempts (primary, same-params, reduced-scope) before being marked failed-but-continuing; 3 total task failures in one session trips a mission-wide abort that refuses further work until the policy object is reset.
Logger: every session produces exactly 3 artifacts (SQLite WAL DB, full-fidelity JSONL, markdown summary) under a date-hierarchical path; finalize() is idempotent and safe to call twice.

Watchdog: three independent detectors (live sliding-window repetition hash, post-hoc n-gram loop-failure classifier, heartbeat-gap timer) plus a resource sampler are purely observational/callback-based — none of them terminate a process or call themselves; the caller is contractually responsible for acting on the fired callback.

Guardrails: every file read/write in the system is expected to pass through check_read()/check_write() first; an excluded-pattern match cannot be overridden by any approval marker; writes to even allowed paths are rejected without an explicit truthy approval; the module refuses to operate at all (raises at construction) if config/paths.yaml is absent, rather than defaulting open.

HierarchyEnforcer: agent output is scanned for credential/PII leakage and named Golden Rule violations before being treated as clean; matched credential/PII text is never stored unredacted in a Violation (only a SHA-256 fingerprint + length), specifically to prevent violation logs/telemetry from becoming a second leak path.

faith_builder: a Project Faith may specialize but must never contradict its Universal Faith (checked via paired regex antipatterns); assembly refuses outright if EXCLUSIONS.md is empty; every assembled Faith's provenance header records the sha256 of its Universal source, overlay source, and each shared block version, so drift is auditable after the fact; writes are atomic (tmp file + os.replace).

substrate_reasoning: an Executor's approval request only reaches a human when the 5-step protocol (hierarchy -> substrate -> first-principles -> novelty) fails to resolve it, or when it matches the §10.5 always-escalate list (Golden Rule/Hard Exclusion/budget/Prime-Directive changes, irreversible substrate writes, or any Hard-Exclusion-boundary touch) — and that list is checked against the request's own classification/hierarchy data, not just a caller-supplied flag, specifically so a forgetful caller can't bypass it.
